arxiv-2209-01726.title: Johari-Goldstein β \beta relaxation in glassy dynamics originates from two-scale energy landscape
arxiv-2209-01726.creator: Kumpei Shiraishi, Hideyuki Mizuno, Atsushi Ikeda
arxiv-2209-01726.description: Abstract Supercooled liquids undergo complicated structural relaxation processes, which have been a long-standing problem in both experimental and theoretical aspects of condensed matter physics. In particular, past experiments universally observed for many types of molecular liquids that relaxation dynamics separated into two distinct processes at low temperatures.

arxiv-2210-00136.title: IMB-NAS: Neural Architecture Search for Imbalanced Datasets
arxiv-2210-00136.creator: Rahul Duggal, Sheng-Yun Peng, Hao Zhou, Duen Horng Chau
arxiv-2210-00136.description: Abstract Class imbalance is a ubiquitous phenomenon occurring in real world data distributions. To overcome its detrimental effect on training accurate classifiers, existing work follows three major directions: class re-balancing, information transfer, and representation learning. In this paper, we propose a new and complementary direction for improving performance on long tailed datasets—optimising the backbone architecture through neural architecture search (NAS).

arxiv-2302-07168.title: Arc-Flags Meet Trip-Based Public Transit Routing
arxiv-2302-07168.creator: Ernestine Großmann, Jonas Sauer, Christian Schulz, Patrick Steil
arxiv-2302-07168.description: Abstract We present Arc-Flag TB , a journey planning algorithm for public transit networks which combines Trip-Based Public Transit Routing (TB) [ 21 ] with the Arc-Flags [ 17 ] speedup technique. Compared to previous attempts to apply Arc-Flags to public transit networks, which saw limited success, our approach uses stronger pruning rules to reduce the search space.

arxiv-2310-11041.title: Weak-field regime of scalar-tensor theories with an instantaneous mode
arxiv-2310-11041.creator: Tsutomu Kobayashi, Takashi Hiramatsu
arxiv-2310-11041.description: Abstract Higher-order scalar-tensor theories having an instantaneous mode do not develop the Ostrogradsky instability even if a seemingly dangerous mode is present. Such theories satisfy only partially the degeneracy conditions that are usually imposed to remove the dangerous mode completely, and are dubbed as U-DHOST theories. We study weak gravitational fields sourced by nonrelativistic matter distributions in U-DHOST theories.

arxiv-2404-07907.title: On orthogonality to uniquely ergodic systems
arxiv-2404-07907.creator: M. Górska, M. Lemańczyk, T. de la Rue
arxiv-2404-07907.description: Abstract We solve Boshernitzan’s problem of characterization (in terms of so called Furstenberg systems) of bounded sequences that are orthogonal to all uniquely ergodic systems. As a step toward this solution, we provide a characterization of automorphisms which are disjoint from all ergodic ones as those whose a.a. ergodic components form a family of pairwise disjoint automorphisms.

arxiv-2407-02284.title: Renard: A Modular Pipeline for Extracting Character Networks from Narrative Texts
arxiv-2407-02284.creator: Arthur Amalvy, Vincent Labatut, Richard Dufour
arxiv-2407-02284.description: Abstract Summary Renard ( Relationships Extraction from NARrative Documents ) is a Python library that allows users to define custom natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract character networks from narrative texts. Contrary to the few existing tools, Renard can extract dynamic networks, as well as the more common static networks.

arxiv-2411-01558.title: Adaptive Conformal Inference by Particle Filtering under Hidden Markov Models
arxiv-2411-01558.creator: Xiaoyi Su, Zhixin Zhou, Rui Luo
arxiv-2411-01558.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xiaoyi Su, Zhixin Zhou, Rui Luo. Conformal inference is a statistical method used to construct prediction sets for point predictors, providing reliable uncertainty quantification with probability guarantees. This method utilizes historical labeled data to estimate the conformity or nonconformity between predictions and true labels. However, conducting conformal inference for hidden states under hidden Markov models (HMMs) presents a significant challenge, as the hidden state data is unavailable, resulting in the absence of a true label set to serve as a conformal calibration set.

Currently, there are little available data for testing major hypotheses about pica because of methodological limitations and l

pmc-10481750.title: Impact of medical students’ socioeconomic backgrounds on medical school application, admission and migration in Japan: a web-based survey
pmc-10481750.creator: Yasuyuki Suzuki, Koji Tsunekawa, Yuko Takeda, Jennifer Cleland, Takuya Saiki
pmc-10481750.description: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to clarify and compare the socioeconomic backgrounds of medical students with those of other health professions and non-health faculty students in an era of increasing inequity in Japanese society.DesignThis was a quantitative nationwide study. Data were collected by a cross-sectional web-based anonymous questionnaire.

pmc-10695757.title: The Prevalence and Risk Factors of Clostridioides difficile Infection in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: 10-Year South Korean Experience Based on the National Database
pmc-10695757.creator: Eun Mi Song, Arum Choi, Sukil Kim, Sung Hoon Jung
pmc-10695757.description: BackgroundFew studies evaluate the epidemiology and risk factors of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) in Asian patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We investigated the year-end prevalence, cumulative incidence and risk factors of CDI in Asian patients with IBD using a large-scale population-based cohort in Korea.

pmc-11485481.title: Management of Pulmonary Toxicities Associated with Systemic Therapy in Non Small Cell Lung Cancer
pmc-11485481.creator: Marko Velimirovic, Matthew Brignola, Emily Chheng, Michael Smith, Khaled A Hassan
pmc-11485481.description: Opinion StatementDrug-induced pneumonitis is a common adverse event that may occur during lung cancer systemic therapy. The incidence/prevalence of this side effect has increased due to recent extensive use of immunotherapy. Although pneumonitis prevalence is increased with the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors, it is also associated with chemotherapy and targeted therapy.

pmc-11634362.title: Coexistent sickle cell anemia and autoimmune hemolytic anemia in two adolescents
pmc-11634362.creator: Vinícius Reis Soares, Bruna Paccola Blanco, Carla Luana Dinardo, Marlene Pereira Garanito
pmc-11634362.description: The development of alloantibodies or autoantibodies is a complication observed in sickle cell disease. Autoimmunization occurs in 7.6-12% of chronically or intermittently transfused patients with sickle cell disease; however, the clinical implications of autoAbs are unclear. Few studies have focused on pediatric sickle cell disease and autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

pmc-12504671.title: CT-based study on the safety margin of the anteromedial portal in elbow arthroscopy
pmc-12504671.creator: Tobias Seidel, Sebastian Wegmann, Maximilian Weber, Tim Leschinger, Lars Peter Müller, Michael Hackl
pmc-12504671.description: With the increasing use of elbow arthroscopy, there is a growing concern about the risk of injury to neural structures, particularly the median nerve, when the anteromedial portal is created. This risk, which was previously underestimated, underscores the need for a guide to safe access that can significantly impact surgical practices and patient outcomes.

pmc-12564538.title: Impact of Homophily in Adherence to Anti-Epidemic Measures on the Spread of Infectious Diseases in Social Networks
pmc-12564538.creator: Piotr Bentkowski, Tomasz Gubiec, Lazaros Gallos
pmc-12564538.description: We investigate how homophily in adherence to anti-epidemic measures affects the final size of epidemics in social networks. Using a modified SIR model, we divide agents into two behavioral groups—compliant and non-compliant—and introduce transmission probabilities that depend asymmetrically on the behavior of both the infected and susceptible individuals.

pmc-12717453.title: Can a Mate‐Finding Allee Effect Be Elicited to Help Eradicate Invasive Mammals?
pmc-12717453.creator: Dean P Anderson, Sam Gillingham, M Cecilia Latham, A David M Latham
pmc-12717453.description: The Allee effect is an important ecological process that has implications for extinction of endangered species and for assisting the management of invasive species. Few instances of Allee effects have been quantified in nature due to the adaptive resilience of species and the difficulty in empirically linking ecological mechanisms to population change.

pmc-12755734.title: Impact of injection scheduling on CO2 migration and trapping efficiency in the Johansen formation
pmc-12755734.creator: Hai T. Nguyen
pmc-12755734.description: Injection scheduling is increasingly considered as an operational lever for optimizing carbon dioxide (CO2) storage in saline aquifers, yet its long-term impact on trapping efficiency at field scale remains uncertain. This study employs a field-calibrated vertical equilibrium model of the Johansen formation, offshore Norway, to compare four injection strategies: constant, ramped, pulsed, and low steady, under equal total injected mass.

pmc-13267544.title: Scavenger receptor–mediated lung-targeted delivery of anti-miR-155 oligoDNA nanomicelles with curcumin for acute lung injury therapy
pmc-13267544.creator: Minji Kang, Jihun Oh, Eunjy Kim, Minhyung Lee
pmc-13267544.description: Antisense oligonucleotides offer a powerful strategy for suppressing pro-inflammatory microRNAs, but efficient long-term delivery after systemic administration remains challenging. In this study, we developed a self-assembling oligoDNA-nanomicelle (OD-micelle) platform to simultaneously deliver antisense oligoDNA targeting miR-155 and curcumin, a hydrophobic anti-inflammatory agent, to the lung.

pmc-13285580.title: Durable mid‐term survivorship after proximal ACL repair with suture augmentation in a middle‐aged cohort: A risk factor analysis
pmc-13285580.creator: Anna Patricia Egert, Kristian Nikolaus Schneider, Georg Gosheger, Jan Christoph Theil, Jan Frederic Weller, Alexander Klug, Georg Ahlbäumer
pmc-13285580.description: PurposeArthroscopic primary repair of proximal anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears with suture augmentation (SA) provides a ligament‐preserving alternative to reconstruction. Evidence on mid‐term durability and associated risk factors for revision remains limited. This study evaluated revision‐free survival at a minimum follow‐up of 72 months and identified risk factors for revision.

pmc-13388834.title: Association of healthy lifestyle and physical fitness in children: a nationwide population-based cross-sectional study
pmc-13388834.creator: Mengmeng Fan, Yuan Liu, Jie Shen, Changzheng Yuan, Xiaojian Yin, Min Hou
pmc-13388834.description: ObjectiveAlthough a healthy lifestyle is closely linked to various health outcomes in children and adolescents, its specific connection to physical fitness remains poorly understood.MethodsThis nationwide cross-sectional study evaluated data from 60,177 children across 27 provinces in China from 2015 to 2016.

pmc-13406019.creator: Marco Giancola, Laura Piccardi, Simonetta D’Amico, Raffaella Nori, Paola Guariglia, Emanuele Cardella, Massimiliano Palmiero

pmc-13688745.title: Key factors influencing the adoption of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) among commercial sex workers in Nekemte Town, Western Ethiopia, 2023
pmc-13688745.creator: Matiyos Lema, Amanuel Lamessa, Edosa Tesfaye Geta, Adisu Tekle
pmc-13688745.description: BackgroundThe rate of HIV among female sex workers in Ethiopia ranges from 14% to 28%, significantly surpassing the adult prevalence rate in the country, which stands at only 0.9%. Female sex workers must adopt pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) due to their heightened vulnerability to HIV, attributed to factors such as inconsistent condom use and frequent encounters with multiple sexual partners.
